headline: 0 on-chain addresses catalogued; Sui chain not supported by DeFiPunkd API; governance role structure documented but no deployed package IDs or multisig addresses found in fetched sources.
short_headline: 0 addresses found; Sui unsupported by API

findings.text: D1: Sui blockchain uses Suiscan/Suivision as block explorers, neither of which is supported by DeFiPunkd's on-chain read API (chainIds 1,10,56,130,137,324,8453,42161,43114,59144,81457,534352,11155111 only). No EVM explorer applies. Direct fetch of Sui explorers was not attempted because no Sui explorer URL appeared in prior search results.

D2: Official GitBook documentation at https://current-finance.gitbook.io/current/ was indexed via llms.txt. No dedicated 'Deployed Contracts' or 'Addresses' page exists in the index. The Buildkit docs (https://current-finance.gitbook.io/buildkit) are referenced as containing asset and governance parameters, but that URL was not fetchable in this run (did not appear in prior search/fetch results).

D3: Audit reports page fetched. Eight audits listed: Sherlock public bug bounty audit contest, Movebit governance audit, Asymptotic leverage+governance audit, Asymptotic lending audit, Pebble (Current) lending audit (firm unlisted), Asymptotic formal verification report, Movebit FLP audit, Scalebit penetration testing report. All linked as GitBook blob files (non-direct PDF URLs), not fetchable as evidence. No contract addresses extracted from the audit scope tables — audit files themselves were not accessible.

D4: GitHub org slug is 'current-finance' per per-protocol context, but https://github.com/current-finance did not appear in search results and was rejected by the fetch allowlist when attempted directly. No repo names, commit SHAs, or deployment artifact files could be retrieved.
D5: Protocol is single-chain (Sui only). No multi-chain enumeration required. Sui is not supported by DeFiPunkd's /api/contract/read or /api/safe/owners endpoints.
D6: No factory addresses were discovered in any fetched source. No factory enumeration was possible.

D7: Technical Details doc describes three governance roles: Watcher (immediate pause/circuit-break, no delay), Param-Modifier (new assets, config changes, 24h timelock + 12h execution window), SuperAdmin (role membership only). Doc states capabilities are 'held by an off-chain multisig' but does not name or address any multisig. No addresses available for taxonomy.

D8: Zero addresses catalogued. No admin_addresses[] entries can be produced with citation. All governance/multisig addresses remain unknown pending access to GitHub deployment artifacts or Sui explorer data.

rationale.verdict: Discovery is incomplete due to two compounding blockers: (1) Sui is not supported by DeFiPunkd's on-chain read API, eliminating all programmatic on-chain reads; (2) the GitHub org and Buildkit docs URLs were not reachable via fetch allowlist in this run, eliminating the primary source of deployed package IDs. The fetched GitBook docs confirm the protocol exists and describe its governance role architecture (Watcher / Param-Modifier / SuperAdmin with multisig), but no contract addresses or package IDs were found in any fetched page. Grade is unknown; downstream runs should prioritize fetching https://current-finance.gitbook.io/buildkit and https://github.com/current-finance to discover Sui package IDs.

protocol_metadata.about: Current Finance is a capital market for global tokenized yield built on the Sui blockchain, connecting yield originators with on-chain liquidity for real-world asset exposure. Users can lend assets into isolated lending markets, loop yield positions using flash-loan-powered Multiply, or trade with leverage via Margin — all connected through a shared audited risk engine. The protocol features Pyth-based oracle pricing with staleness and confidence-interval guards, per-asset outflow rate limiting, and a three-tier governance model (Watcher, Param-Modifier, SuperAdmin) with asymmetric delay — risk-reducing actions execute immediately while risk-increasing parameter changes require a 24-hour timelock.
